title: MuscleMemory cuts Codex tool calls 30% by reusing skills learned from passing tests
summary: Coding agents relearn the same steps every session. MuscleMemory watches agent sessions, saves how tasks were done once tests pass, and hands a short note next time, which its author reports cut tokens, tool calls and time in Codex benchmarks.
agent_role: The coding agent does the task; MuscleMemory captures successful sessions as skills and injects notes later. A human must approve each skill before agents see it.
outcome: Author reports a benchmark with real Codex sessions cut input tokens 25.5%, tool calls 30.4% and time 28.2% with all tasks passing; an early Claude Code run cut input tokens 43.5%.
what_they_did: The author built hooks for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor that record agent sessions. When tests pass after the last change, it learns a skill: files to change, the verifying test and pitfalls. Skills must pass two later checks and a human Keep before reuse, and they are shared across agents.
how_it_went: The author reports 25.5% fewer input tokens, 30.4% fewer tool calls and 28.2% less time on Codex benchmarks, and on a small SWE-bench Django run Codex solved as many issues with about half the tokens.
worth_knowing: Benchmarks cover repeat tasks on three controlled codebases and the Claude Code run is small; cross-repository recall is untested.
prompt: Set up MuscleMemory for this project following its install docs, connect it to [your agent], then work on [task] as usual. After the tests pass, show me the skill it proposes to learn and wait for my approval in the dashboard before keeping it.

curation.rationale: A tool, but the README reports concrete benchmark runs with Codex and Claude Code sessions and a reproduce script. It is still early and the runs are small.
